relationship.statement: For small angles, a pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, not on bob mass. Larger release angles increase swing speed and slightly lengthen the period.
assumptions: Air resistance and pivot friction are neglected.
The string is massless and stays taut.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot to the center of the bob.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle pulled aside from the vertical rest position.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the hanging weight attached to the string.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration at Earth's surface.

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time taken to complete one full back-and-forth swing.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete back-and-forth swings per second.

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Fastest speed of the bob at the bottom of the swing.

quantities.label: Mechanical energy
quantities.meaning: Total potential and kinetic energy driving the swing.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = inputs.L; var theta0Deg = inputs.theta_0; var m = 1.0; var g = 9.81; var theta0 = theta0Deg * Math.PI / 180; var T_small = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var a = 1; var b = Math.cos(theta0 / 2); for (var i = 0; i < 6; i++) { var an = 0.5 * (a + b); b = Math.sqrt(a * b); a = an; } var T = T_small / a; var f = 1 / T; var v_max = Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(theta0))); var E_total = m * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(theta0)); var omega0 = Math.sqrt(g / L); var angle_small = theta0 * Math.cos(omega0 * t); var steps = t > 0 ? Math.ceil(t / 0.02) : 0; var dt = steps > 0 ? t / steps : 0; var th = theta0; var om = 0; var c = -g / L; for (var j = 0; j < steps; j++) { var k1t = om; var k1o = c * Math.sin(th); var k2t = om + 0.5 * dt * k1o; var k2o = c * Math.sin(th + 0.5 * dt * k1t); var k3t = om + 0.5 * dt * k2o; var k3o = c * Math.sin(th + 0.5 * dt * k2t); var k4t = om + dt * k3o; var k4o = c * Math.sin(th + dt * k3t); th += (dt / 6) * (k1t + 2 * k2t + 2 * k3t + k4t); om += (dt / 6) * (k1o + 2 * k2o + 2 * k3o + k4o); } var x_bob = L * Math.sin(th); var y_bob = -L * Math.cos(th); var x_small = L * Math.sin(angle_small); var y_small = -L * Math.cos(angle_small); return { T: T, f: f, v_max: v_max, E_total: E_total, T_small: T_small, x_bob: x_bob, y_bob: y_bob, x_small: x_small, y_small: y_small, plumb_y: -L * 1.05, angle_deg: th * 180 / Math.PI, angle_small_deg: angle_small * 180 / Math.PI, is_small_angle: theta0Deg <= 15, is_large_angle: theta0Deg >= 45 }; }

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Adjust string length and release angle to compare a real pendulum against its small-angle ideal. Watch how period, speed, energy, and timing respond.
lesson.instructions: Move the String length slider to stretch or shorten the pendulum, and drag Release angle to pull it higher. Compare the real bob and graph line against the small-angle reference.
lesson.goal: See that string length sets the small-angle period while larger release angles boost speed, energy, and slightly lengthen the swing period.
